heading: Population Health & Ethics
lo_model: one LO per item for now; shared objectives later

items.question_text: A patient is given another patient's insulin dose and becomes hypoglycaemic. He recovers. The consultant says to say nothing unless he asks, because an apology is an admission of liability. Open disclosure is the discussion of an incident that resulted in harm. He is told what happened and what will be done to prevent a repeat. Tell him what happened, the effect, and what has changed. An apology for the harm is appropriate. What is the most appropriate action?  Silence unless asked is the error. Harm already occurred. An expression of regret is part of the discussion. Notes are not a substitute for telling him.  The duty is to the person affected, not to recruitment numbers or to a quiet file. Apply it.  Nothing in the outcome so far removes the need to disclose, to allow withdrawal, or to report.  Do that now.  A good overall result or a recovered patient does not close the duty.  Recruitment, a quiet file, or a recovered patient does not remove the duty to disclose, to allow withdrawal, or to report.  Apply the rule to the facts in front of you. Do not wait for a complaint or a journal query.
options: Tell him what happened, the effect, and what has changed. An apology for the harm is appropriate
Say nothing. An apology is an admission of liability
Tell him only if he develops lasting injury
Ask the nurse to explain it in the notes and not to the patient
Offer money before any explanation
items.subtopic: Open disclosure tells the patient what happened, what it means, and what will be done. It is not an apology that admits legal liability in a scripted way, and it is not silence.
items.lo_title: Open disclosure follows harm, including intercepted near misses

blueprint.note: Coverage reporting and tie-break only. Not a quota.

items.explanation:
Open disclosure is the discussion of an incident that resulted in harm. He is told what happened and what will be done to prevent a repeat. An expression of regret for the harm is part of that discussion. Staying silent unless asked is the error.

B. Say nothing. An apology is an admission of liability
Silence is not the safeguard.

A. Tell him what happened, the effect, and what has changed. An apology for the harm is appropriate
This is the action.

C. Tell him only if he develops lasting injury
Harm already occurred.

D. Ask the nurse to explain it in the notes and not to the patient
The notes are not a substitute for telling him.

E. Offer money before any explanation
Payment is not the first step, and it is not a substitute for disclosure.
items.diagnosis_explanation: Tell him. Do not wait for him to ask, and do not treat an apology as forbidden.
key_takeaways: Open disclosure follows harm.
Saying nothing is not a legal strategy.

items.question_text: A child is almost given a tenfold morphine dose. A second nurse stops it before any drug is given. The family were not in the room. A registrar says disclosure is unnecessary because nothing was administered. An error that reached the point of administration, even if intercepted, is disclosed and reported. Tell the family about the intercepted error, and report it internally. What is the most appropriate course?  No drug given does not make it invisible. Internal reporting does not replace telling the family. Blame without system reporting misses the point.  The duty is to the person affected, not to recruitment numbers or to a quiet file. Apply it.  Nothing in the outcome so far removes the need to disclose, to allow withdrawal, or to report.  Do that now.  A good overall result or a recovered patient does not close the duty.  Recruitment, a quiet file, or a recovered patient does not remove the duty to disclose, to allow withdrawal, or to report.  Apply the rule to the facts in front of you. Do not wait for a complaint or a journal query.
options: No disclosure. A near miss is an internal matter only
Tell the family about the intercepted error, and report it internally
Tell them only if they complain about the delay
Discipline the first nurse and close the file
Document 'dose checked' and move on
items.subtopic: A near miss that reached the patient is still discussed. No harm does not mean no disclosure.
items.lo_title: Open disclosure follows harm, including intercepted near misses

blueprint.note: Coverage reporting and tie-break only. Not a quota.

items.explanation:
An error that reached the point of administration, even if intercepted, is disclosed in terms the family can understand, and is reported so the system changes. No drug given does not make it invisible.

A. No disclosure. A near miss is an internal matter only
Internal reporting does not replace telling them.

B. Tell the family about the intercepted error, and report it internally
This is the course.

C. Tell them only if they complain about the delay
A complaint is not the trigger.

D. Discipline the first nurse and close the file
Blame without system reporting misses the point.

E. Document 'dose checked' and move on
A false reassuring entry hides the event.
items.diagnosis_explanation: Tell the family and report it. Intercepted is not the same as never happened.
key_takeaways: A near miss that reached the bedside is disclosed.
Blame is not the whole response.

items.question_text: A patient is asked to join a drug trial. The registrar says his surgery will be scheduled sooner if he enrols, and delayed if he declines. Consent to research is voluntary. Linking the timing of needed surgery to enrolment is coercion. Coercive. Care must not be conditional on joining the trial. What is the most appropriate view?  A free drug does not repair a link between enrolment and the timing of surgery. Public patients are not a lesser group. Care is not a reward for saying yes.  The duty is to the person affected, not to recruitment numbers or to a quiet file. Apply it.  Nothing in the outcome so far removes the need to disclose, to allow withdrawal, or to report.  Do that now.  A good overall result or a recovered patient does not close the duty.  Recruitment, a quiet file, or a recovered patient does not remove the duty to disclose, to allow withdrawal, or to report.  Apply the rule to the facts in front of you. Do not wait for a complaint or a journal query.
options: Acceptable. Incentives for recruitment are unrestricted
Acceptable if the trial drug is free
Coercive. Care must not be conditional on joining the trial
Acceptable if the surgeon agrees
Acceptable for public patients only
items.subtopic: Research participation is voluntary. Clinical care does not depend on saying yes.
items.lo_title: Research consent is voluntary and withdrawal needs no reason

blueprint.note: Coverage reporting and tie-break only. Not a quota.

items.explanation:
Consent to research is voluntary. Linking the timing of needed surgery to enrolment is coercion. A free drug does not repair that link.

A. Acceptable. Incentives for recruitment are unrestricted
They are not.

C. Coercive. Care must not be conditional on joining the trial
This is the view.

B. Acceptable if the trial drug is free
Cost is not the problem.

D. Acceptable if the surgeon agrees
Agreement does not make coercion valid.

E. Acceptable for public patients only
Public patients are not a lesser group.
items.diagnosis_explanation: Do not tie his operation to enrolment.
key_takeaways: Research consent is voluntary.
Care is not a reward for saying yes.

items.question_text: A woman in a randomised drug trial wants to stop. She will not say why. The coordinator says she must give a reason, and that withdrawal means she loses her outpatient follow-up. Withdrawal is a right. No reason is required. Clinical care is not cancelled because she leaves the study. She may withdraw without a reason, and her clinical care continues. What is the most appropriate response?  Further research visits cannot be compelled. A reason is not a condition. Clinical care is separate from the trial. Let her stop.  The duty is to the person affected, not to recruitment numbers or to a quiet file. Apply it.  Nothing in the outcome so far removes the need to disclose, to allow withdrawal, or to report.  Do that now.  A good overall result or a recovered patient does not close the duty.  Recruitment, a quiet file, or a recovered patient does not remove the duty to disclose, to allow withdrawal, or to report.  Apply the rule to the facts in front of you. Do not wait for a complaint or a journal query.
options: She must give a reason. Otherwise the data are invalid
She may withdraw only before the second dose
Withdrawal is allowed only if the chief investigator agrees
She may withdraw without a reason, and her clinical care continues
She can withdraw from the drug but must still attend research visits
items.subtopic: A participant may withdraw from a trial at any time, without giving a reason, and without losing clinical care.

items.explanation:
Withdrawal is a right. No reason is required. Clinical care is not cancelled because she leaves the study. Further research visits cannot be compelled.

A reason is not a condition.

D. She may withdraw without a reason, and her clinical care continues
This is the response.

B. She may withdraw only before the second dose

C. Withdrawal is allowed only if the chief investigator agrees

E. She can withdraw from the drug but must still attend research visits

items.diagnosis_explanation: Let her stop. No reason, and her care continues.
key_takeaways: Withdrawal needs no reason.
Clinical care is separate from the trial.

items.question_text: The principal investigator owns 30% of the company making the trial device. The consent form does not mention this. He says disclosure would worry patients and reduce recruitment. Participants are told about interests that could influence the study. Disclose the ownership in the consent. Do not hide a financial interest. What is the most appropriate action?  Telling only the committee, or only in the final paper, leaves the consent incomplete. Moving the shares to a spouse does not remove the interest.  The duty is to the person affected, not to recruitment numbers or to a quiet file. Apply it.  Nothing in the outcome so far removes the need to disclose, to allow withdrawal, or to report.  Do that now.  A good overall result or a recovered patient does not close the duty.  Recruitment, a quiet file, or a recovered patient does not remove the duty to disclose, to allow withdrawal, or to report.  Apply the rule to the facts in front of you. Do not wait for a complaint or a journal query.
options: Leave it out. Recruitment matters more than ownership
Disclose it only to the ethics committee, not to participants
Disclose it after the trial, in the paper
Transfer the shares to a spouse and do not disclose
Disclose the ownership in the consent. Do not hide a financial interest
items.subtopic: A conflict of interest in research is declared. Ownership of the sponsoring company is not omitted from the consent.
items.lo_title: Research conflict of interest and serious adverse events are disclosed

blueprint.note: Coverage reporting and tie-break only. Not a quota.

items.explanation:
Participants are told about interests that could influence the study. Ownership is such an interest. Telling only the committee, or only in the final paper, leaves the consent incomplete. Moving the shares to a spouse does not remove the interest.

A. Leave it out. Recruitment matters more than ownership
Recruitment is not a reason to hide it.

E. Disclose the ownership in the consent. Do not hide a financial interest
This is the action.

B. Disclose it only to the ethics committee, not to participants
The participant is the person consenting.

C. Disclose it after the trial, in the paper
Too late for consent.

D. Transfer the shares to a spouse and do not disclose
A related-party holding is still an interest.
items.diagnosis_explanation: Put the ownership in the consent. Recruitment is not a reason to hide it.
key_takeaways: A financial interest is disclosed to participants.
A spouse's holding does not erase it.

items.question_text: In a surgical trial, one participant dies of a pulmonary embolus a week after the new procedure. The investigator plans to mention it only if the journal asks, because the other 40 patients did well. Death is a serious adverse event. It is reported promptly. Report the death as a serious adverse event, to the sponsor and the ethics committee, now. What is the most appropriate action?  A favourable overall result does not delay or hide a death. Reclassifying or deleting the case without review is misconduct. Report it now.  The duty is to the person affected, not to recruitment numbers or to a quiet file. Apply it.  Nothing in the outcome so far removes the need to disclose, to allow withdrawal, or to report.  Do that now.  A good overall result or a recovered patient does not close the duty.  Recruitment, a quiet file, or a recovered patient does not remove the duty to disclose, to allow withdrawal, or to report.  Apply the rule to the facts in front of you. Do not wait for a complaint or a journal query.
options: Report the death as a serious adverse event, to the sponsor and the ethics committee, now
Wait for the journal. One death does not change a positive trial
Report it only at the end-of-study meeting
Reclassify the death as unrelated without review
Remove that participant from the analysis
items.subtopic: An adverse event in a trial is reported. A good outcome overall does not bury a serious harm.
items.lo_title: Research conflict of interest and serious adverse events are disclosed

blueprint.note: Coverage reporting and tie-break only. Not a quota.

items.explanation:
Death is a serious adverse event. It is reported promptly through the trial's safety pathway. A favourable overall result does not delay or hide it. Reclassifying or deleting the case without review is misconduct.

B. Wait for the journal. One death does not change a positive trial
The journal is not the safety system.

A. Report the death as a serious adverse event, to the sponsor and the ethics committee, now
This is the action.

C. Report it only at the end-of-study meeting
Serious events are not saved for the end.

D. Reclassify the death as unrelated without review
Relatedness is reviewed, not assumed away.

E. Remove that participant from the analysis
Deleting a death corrupts the trial.
items.diagnosis_explanation: Report the death now. Do not wait for the journal.
key_takeaways: A trial death is a serious adverse event.
It is reported promptly, not buried in a good result.
